decisions.reason: This flagship electrometer remains tightly tied to the firm's core dosimetry and radiation-therapy QA franchise, so management would be very unlikely to withdraw it.
The CT image quality phantom extends the established medical-imaging QA offer with a straightforward adjacent product that fits the firm's broad portfolio and growth direction.
Although this mammography phantom is somewhat farther from the historic core, it still supports the firm's expansion in imaging QA and as a hardware phantom is not especially burdensome to maintain.

This full field mammography phantom is a more niche and distant extension than the core radiation-therapy line, so it carries a somewhat higher withdrawal risk but is still worth retaining while the imaging QA portfolio is being built out.
As a flagship multi-model imaging QA line that matches the firm's stated move toward integrated measurement-based QA, it is highly likely to stay on the market and receive continued support.
